summary:
Disputed by the supplier: GnuTLS can trust a certificate on its Common
Name when the Subject Alternative Name holds an SRV otherName whose value
is an OCTET STRING, because the undecodable entry is reported as a generic
otherName and does not preclude the CN fallback. The CVE record notes that
GnuTLS does not consider this an actionable vulnerability, because its
threat model (SECURITY.md) excludes attacks that need control of material
inside the trust boundary (trusted CAs and the certificates they issue).
There is no upstream fix: the only proposed change, third-party MR !2165,
is unmerged. Debian rates it unimportant and leaves it unfixed in every
suite.
